name: Coronary heart disease, lifestyle and cancer

terms.definition: A disease in which layers of fatty material build up in the coronary arteries, narrowing them and reducing the flow of blood, so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.
terms.examiner: Treated with stents, statins or, for faulty valves, a valve replacement.

terms.definition: A mesh tube inserted into an artery to keep it open.
terms.examiner: A drawback is the risk of a blood clot forming.

terms.definition: A drug that lowers blood cholesterol, slowing the build-up of fatty material in the arteries.
terms.examiner: Must be taken long term and can have side effects.

terms.definition: A disease that cannot be passed from one person to another, such as heart disease or most cancers.
terms.examiner: Risk factors increase the chance, but do not guarantee the disease.

terms.definition: Something linked to a greater chance of a disease, such as smoking, obesity or alcohol.
terms.examiner: A correlation does not prove the factor causes the disease.

terms.definition: A growth of abnormal cells contained in one area, usually within a membrane; it does not invade other parts of the body.
terms.examiner: Benign tumours can still cause harm by pressing on organs.

terms.definition: A cancer: a tumour that invades neighbouring tissues and spreads in the blood to form secondary tumours.
terms.examiner: Cancer is the result of uncontrolled cell division.
